This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners, learned counsel for the Opposite Party No.2-Informant and learned counsel for the State-Opposite Party No.1.
Perused the CRLMC application as well as the documents annexed thereto.

3. By filing the present CRLMC application, the Petitioners have prayed for quashing of the F.I.R. in Badagad P.S. Case No.431 dated 14.12.2021 under Annexure-1 to the application.
4.

Mr. S. Pattnaik, learned counsel for the Petitioners, at the outset, contended that the Opposite Party No.2-Informant lodged an F.I.R. at Badagad Police Station, Bhubaneswar, which was registered as Badagad P.S. Case No.431 of 2021, for alleged commission of offences under Sections 420/341/323/294/354/506/34 of I.P.C.

He further contended that due to a misunderstanding between the Petitioners and the Opposite Party No.2-Informant, the present case has been registered at the instance of the Opposite Party No.2-Informant.
He further submitted that the Petitioners had taken money from the Opposite Party No.2-Informant to sell a piece of land.

sentences.text:
the sale deed could not be executed due to lack of sanction by the G.A. & P.G. Department,
Government of Odisha, the Petitioners could not sell the land.
The delay in the process created a doubt in the mind of the Opposite Party No.2-Informant, as a result of which, the present criminal case has been filed implicating the Petitioners as an accused.

Learned counsel for the Petitioners further contended that in the meantime after refusal of grant of permission by the G.A.&P.G.
Department, the Petitioners have already refunded the money to the Opposite Party No.2-Informant and the matter has been amicably resolved between the parties.
5. Mr. B. Moharana, learned counsel appearing for the Opposite Party No.2-Inforamnt filed an affidavit in Court today sworn before the Oath Commissioner of this Court.

6. On perusal of such affidavit, it appears that the Opposite Party No.2-Informant has received a sum of Rs.25,40,000/- towards full and final settlement of the money which he had given to the Petitioners for the alleged sale transaction.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the Opposite Party No.2- Informant further contended that the aforesaid money has been received towards full and final settlement and that the Opposite Party No.2-Informant does not have any specific grievance.
He further submitted that since the dispute has been amicably settled outside the court, the Opposite Party No.2-Informant is not interested to pursue the matter further.

Accordingly, learned counsel for the Opposite Party No.2-Informant also supported the stand of the Petitioners to quash the F.I.R.
8.
Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, contended that since the issue has been resolved between the parties, he will have no objection in the event the F.I.R. is quashed.

9. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on a careful examination of the background facts, further taking into consideration the subsequent development that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties and that the Informant has received back the entire amount as has been indicated in her affidavit filed in Court today and both the parties have no more interested in continuing the criminal proceeding further, this Court is of the view that further continuance of the present criminal proceeding would be an abuse of process of law and that the same would not be in the larger interest of justice.

10. Accordingly, the Criminal Miscellaneous Case is allowed and the entire criminal proceeding launched against the Petitioners vide C.T. Case No.6949 of 2021, arising out of Badagad P.S. Case No.431 dated 14.12.2021, pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C.- IV, Bhubaneswar,
is hereby quashed, so far as the present Petitioners are concerned.

The learned J.M.F.C.-IV, Bhubaneswar or the court in seisin over the matter shall, on receipt of this order/production of the certified copy of this order, close the proceeding in the aforesaid case in compliance of this order.
(Aditya Kumar Mohapatra) Judge Debasis ) Smt. Shantilata Patra @ Santi vs ) State Of Odisha .....
